## Overview

This document

1. loads every completed 2025–26 regular-season game,
2. fits a **Bradley-Terry model with a home-court advantage term**,
3. simulates the **entire season (1,230 games), the play-in tournament, and the full playoffs** at least 10,000 times, and
4. keeps *every team's* result in every simulation (wins, conference rank, playoff seed, rounds won), so you can slice it any way you like later.

**The model.** For a game with home team $i$ and away team $j$:

$$
\operatorname{logit} P(\text{home wins}) = h + \theta_i - \theta_j
$$

where $\theta$ is a team strength and $h$ is a single league-wide home-court advantage.
It is fit as a logistic regression (the regular season only, so the playoffs are
*out of sample* for the model).

**Parameter uncertainty.** Ratings are estimated from only 82 games per team. If we simulated with the
point estimates, every simulated season would assume we know each team's true strength exactly, which
overstates how predictable the league is. Instead, each simulation first draws a fresh set of
$(h, \theta)$ from the model's estimated sampling distribution (multivariate normal around the MLE),
then plays out the season. This matters a lot when asking whether a surprising champion is an "anomaly".

## Settings

```{r settings}
N_SIMS             <- 10000     # minimum requested: 10,000
SEED               <- 2026
CHUNK              <- 1000      # sims processed at a time (memory)
PARAM_UNCERTAINTY  <- TRUE      # draw (h, theta) from their sampling distribution each sim
SEASON             <- 2026      # hoopR convention: 2026 = the 2025-26 season
FOCUS_TEAM         <- "New York Knicks"
GAMES_CSV          <- NULL      # optional: path to a CSV with columns
                                #   home, away, home_pts, away_pts   (regular season only)
SIMS_FILE          <- "nba_sims_2026.rds"   # results are saved here for later analysis
```

```{r packages}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(knitr)
# install.packages(c("hoopR")) once if you don't have it (only needed if GAMES_CSV is NULL)
```

## Data

```{r teams}
teams <- tibble::tribble(
  ~team,                     ~conf,
  "Atlanta Hawks",           "East", "Boston Celtics",          "East",
  "Brooklyn Nets",           "East", "Charlotte Hornets",       "East",
  "Chicago Bulls",           "East", "Cleveland Cavaliers",     "East",
  "Detroit Pistons",         "East", "Indiana Pacers",          "East",
  "Miami Heat",              "East", "Milwaukee Bucks",         "East",
  "New York Knicks",         "East", "Orlando Magic",           "East",
  "Philadelphia 76ers",      "East", "Toronto Raptors",         "East",
  "Washington Wizards",      "East",
  "Dallas Mavericks",        "West", "Denver Nuggets",          "West",
  "Golden State Warriors",   "West", "Houston Rockets",         "West",
  "LA Clippers",             "West", "Los Angeles Lakers",      "West",
  "Memphis Grizzlies",       "West", "Minnesota Timberwolves",  "West",
  "New Orleans Pelicans",    "West", "Oklahoma City Thunder",   "West",
  "Phoenix Suns",            "West", "Portland Trail Blazers",  "West",
  "Sacramento Kings",        "West", "San Antonio Spurs",       "West",
  "Utah Jazz",               "West"
) |>
  arrange(team) |>
  mutate(id = row_number(), conf_id = if_else(conf == "East", 1L, 2L))

n_teams <- nrow(teams)
stopifnot(n_teams == 30)
```

```{r load-data}
fix_names <- function(x) recode(x, "Los Angeles Clippers" = "LA Clippers")

if (!is.null(GAMES_CSV)) {
  games <- readr::read_csv(GAMES_CSV, show_col_types = FALSE)
} else {
  raw <- hoopR::load_nba_schedule(seasons = SEASON)
  games <- raw |>
    filter(season_type == 2) |>                      # 2 = regular season
    # Rows ESPN tags as regular season that are NOT part of the 82-game schedule:
    #   * the NBA Cup Championship game and All-Star weekend games
    #   (Cup group play AND Cup quarterfinals/semifinals DO count toward the 82, so they stay.)
    filter(is.na(notes_headline) |
             !grepl("Cup Championship|All-Star", notes_headline, ignore.case = TRUE)) |>
    filter(is.na(type_abbreviation) | !type_abbreviation %in% c("CC", "ALLSTAR")) |>
    # Postponed games leave a 0-0 placeholder row at the original date; the real result
    # appears again as a separate "Makeup from ..." row, so drop the placeholders.
    filter(!is.na(home_score), !is.na(away_score)) |>
    filter(as.numeric(home_score) + as.numeric(away_score) > 0) |>
    transmute(home = home_display_name, away = away_display_name,
              home_pts = as.numeric(home_score), away_pts = as.numeric(away_score))
}

games <- games |>
  mutate(home = fix_names(home), away = fix_names(away))

# Drop non-NBA-team games (All-Star weekend / Rising Stars exhibitions are tagged as
# regular season in some feeds, e.g. "Team Stripes", "Team Stars", "World").
is_real <- games$home %in% teams$team & games$away %in% teams$team
if (any(!is_real)) {
  cat("Dropping", sum(!is_real), "non-team games:",
      paste(unique(c(games$home[!is_real], games$away[!is_real])[
        !(c(games$home[!is_real], games$away[!is_real]) %in% teams$team)]), collapse = ", "), "\n")
}
games <- games[is_real, ]

games <- games |>
  left_join(teams |> select(team, home_id = id), by = c("home" = "team")) |>
  left_join(teams |> select(team, away_id = id), by = c("away" = "team")) |>
  mutate(home_win = as.integer(home_pts > away_pts))

# ---- sanity checks -----------------------------------------------------------
if (anyNA(games$home_id) || anyNA(games$away_id)) {
  stop("Unmatched team names: ",
       paste(unique(c(games$home[is.na(games$home_id)], games$away[is.na(games$away_id)])),
             collapse = ", "))
}
gp <- table(c(games$home_id, games$away_id))
if (nrow(games) != 1230 || any(gp != 82)) {
  warning("Expected 1,230 games and 82 per team, got ", nrow(games),
          " games (per team: ", min(gp), "-", max(gp), "). ",
          "If an NBA Cup final or other non-regular-season game slipped in, drop it before continuing.")
}
```

```{r actual-standings}
actual <- bind_rows(
  games |> transmute(id = home_id, w = home_win),
  games |> transmute(id = away_id, w = 1L - home_win)
) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(actual_wins = sum(w), actual_losses = n() - sum(w), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(teams, by = "id") |>
  group_by(conf) |>
  mutate(actual_conf_rank = rank(-actual_wins, ties.method = "min")) |>   # wins only; no tiebreakers
  ungroup()

cat(nrow(games), "games loaded.\n")
```

## Fit the Bradley-Terry model

The team indicator matrix has +1 for the home team and −1 for the away team. The first team
(alphabetically) is the reference with $\theta = 0$; only differences matter. The intercept is $h$.

```{r fit-bt}
X <- matrix(0, nrow(games), n_teams)
X[cbind(seq_len(nrow(games)), games$home_id)] <-  1
X[cbind(seq_len(nrow(games)), games$away_id)] <- -1
X <- X[, -1, drop = FALSE]

fit <- glm(games$home_win ~ X, family = binomial)

beta_hat <- coef(fit)          # [1] = h, [2:30] = theta for teams 2..30
V        <- vcov(fit)

h_hat     <- unname(beta_hat[1])
theta_hat <- c(0, unname(beta_hat[-1]))

ratings <- teams |>
  mutate(theta = theta_hat - mean(theta_hat),            # centre so the league average = 0
         p_vs_avg_neutral = plogis(theta)) |>
  left_join(actual |> select(id, actual_wins), by = "id") |>
  arrange(desc(theta))

cat(sprintf("Home-court advantage: h = %.3f log-odds -> %.1f%% home win prob between equal teams\n",
            h_hat, 100 * plogis(h_hat)))
```

```{r ratings-table}
ratings |>
  transmute(Team = team, Conf = conf, `Rating (θ)` = round(theta, 3),
            `Win % vs avg team (neutral)` = percent(p_vs_avg_neutral, 0.1),
            `Actual wins` = actual_wins) |>
  kable()
```

A quick calibration check: the model's expected wins from the fitted game probabilities should track actual wins.

```{r calibration}
games$p_hat <- fitted(fit)
exp_w <- bind_rows(
  games |> transmute(id = home_id, p = p_hat),
  games |> transmute(id = away_id, p = 1 - p_hat)
) |> group_by(id) |> summarise(expected_wins = sum(p), .groups = "drop")

calib <- actual |> left_join(exp_w, by = "id")
```

```{r calibration-plot}
ggplot(calib, aes(expected_wins, actual_wins, label = team)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(colour = "#006BB6") +
  geom_text(size = 2.5, vjust = -0.7, check_overlap = TRUE) +
  labs(x = "Model-expected wins", y = "Actual wins",
       title = "Bradley-Terry fit vs. actual regular-season wins")
```

## Simulation engine

Everything is vectorised across simulations: each function takes a vector of teams (one entry per
simulation) and returns a vector of winners. Simplifications to be aware of:

* **Tiebreakers:** regular-season ties are broken randomly (no head-to-head / division rules).
* **Play-in:** 7v8 winner is the 7 seed; loser hosts the winner of 9v10 for the 8 seed. Higher seed hosts.
* **Series:** best-of-7, 2-2-1-1-1, higher seed has home court; the Finals give home court to the team with more regular-season wins.
* **Injuries, rest, trades, and in-season changes in strength** are not modelled. Ratings are constant for the whole season and playoffs.

```{r engine}
# --- draw model parameters for n simulations -------------------------------------
draw_params <- function(n) {
  if (PARAM_UNCERTAINTY) {
    L <- t(chol(V))
    B <- beta_hat + L %*% matrix(rnorm(length(beta_hat) * n), ncol = n)
  } else {
    B <- matrix(beta_hat, nrow = length(beta_hat), ncol = n)
  }
  list(h = B[1, ], Theta = rbind(0, B[-1, , drop = FALSE]))   # Theta: 30 x n
}

# --- one game: `home` and `away` are team-id vectors (length n) ------------------
play_game <- function(home, away, P) {
  n   <- length(home); idx <- seq_len(n)
  eta <- P$h + P$Theta[cbind(home, idx)] - P$Theta[cbind(away, idx)]
  ifelse(runif(n) < plogis(eta), home, away)
}

# --- best-of-7, team `a` has home court (games 1,2,5,7 at a) ---------------------
play_series <- function(a, b, P) {
  n <- length(a); idx <- seq_len(n)
  d <- P$Theta[cbind(a, idx)] - P$Theta[cbind(b, idx)]
  a_home <- c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE)
  wins_a <- 0
  # Playing all 7 games and checking for >= 4 wins gives the same winner distribution
  # as stopping once a team reaches 4.
  for (g in 1:7) wins_a <- wins_a + (runif(n) < plogis(d + if (a_home[g]) P$h else -P$h))
  ifelse(wins_a >= 4, a, b)
}

# --- series where home court goes to the lower "seed score" ----------------------
series_by_seed <- function(t1, s1, t2, s2, P) {
  swap <- s2 < s1
  a <- ifelse(swap, t2, t1); b <- ifelse(swap, t1, t2)
  w <- play_series(a, b, P)
  t1_won <- w == t1
  list(win = w, win_seed = ifelse(t1_won, s1, s2),
       lose = ifelse(t1_won, t2, t1))
}

# --- one conference: play-in + 4 rounds ------------------------------------------
# S: 15 x n matrix of team ids ordered by regular-season rank
sim_conference <- function(S, P, rounds_won, playoff_seed) {
  n <- ncol(S); idx <- seq_len(n)
  rec <- function(mat, team, value) { mat[cbind(team, idx)] <- value; mat }

  # play-in
  w78  <- play_game(S[7, ], S[8, ], P)
  l78  <- ifelse(w78 == S[7, ], S[8, ], S[7, ])
  w910 <- play_game(S[9, ], S[10, ], P)
  g3   <- play_game(l78, w910, P)
  T8   <- rbind(S[1:6, , drop = FALSE], w78, g3)          # row = playoff seed (1..8)
  for (s in 1:8) playoff_seed <- rec(playoff_seed, T8[s, ], s)

  sd <- function(s) rep(s, n)
  # round 1
  a <- series_by_seed(T8[1, ], sd(1), T8[8, ], sd(8), P)
  b <- series_by_seed(T8[4, ], sd(4), T8[5, ], sd(5), P)
  c <- series_by_seed(T8[3, ], sd(3), T8[6, ], sd(6), P)
  d <- series_by_seed(T8[2, ], sd(2), T8[7, ], sd(7), P)
  for (x in list(a, b, c, d)) rounds_won <- rec(rounds_won, x$lose, 0L)
  # round 2
  e <- series_by_seed(a$win, a$win_seed, b$win, b$win_seed, P)
  f <- series_by_seed(c$win, c$win_seed, d$win, d$win_seed, P)
  for (x in list(e, f)) rounds_won <- rec(rounds_won, x$lose, 1L)
  # conference finals
  g <- series_by_seed(e$win, e$win_seed, f$win, f$win_seed, P)
  rounds_won <- rec(rounds_won, g$lose, 2L)

  list(champ = g$win, rounds_won = rounds_won, playoff_seed = playoff_seed)
}

# --- a chunk of n full seasons + postseasons -------------------------------------
simulate_chunk <- function(n, sim_offset = 0L) {
  P   <- draw_params(n)
  idx <- seq_len(n)

  # regular season (actual 1,230-game schedule)
  eta <- P$Theta[games$home_id, , drop = FALSE] - P$Theta[games$away_id, , drop = FALSE]
  eta <- sweep(eta, 2, P$h, "+")
  home_win <- matrix(runif(length(eta)) < plogis(eta), nrow = nrow(eta))
  wins <- rowsum(home_win + 0, games$home_id) + rowsum(1 - home_win, games$away_id)  # 30 x n

  # seeding within each conference (random tiebreak)
  conf_rank    <- matrix(NA_integer_, n_teams, n)
  S_list       <- vector("list", 2)
  for (cf in 1:2) {
    ids <- teams$id[teams$conf_id == cf]
    w   <- wins[ids, , drop = FALSE] + matrix(runif(length(ids) * n, 0, 0.5), nrow = length(ids))
    ord <- apply(w, 2, function(x) order(-x))                     # 15 x n (positions in `ids`)
    S   <- matrix(ids[ord], nrow = length(ids))
    for (r in seq_len(nrow(S))) conf_rank[cbind(S[r, ], idx)] <- r
    S_list[[cf]] <- S
  }

  rounds_won   <- matrix(NA_integer_, n_teams, n)   # NA = missed playoffs
  playoff_seed <- matrix(NA_integer_, n_teams, n)
  east <- sim_conference(S_list[[1]], P, rounds_won, playoff_seed)
  west <- sim_conference(S_list[[2]], P, east$rounds_won, east$playoff_seed)
  rounds_won   <- west$rounds_won
  playoff_seed <- west$playoff_seed

  # NBA Finals: home court to the team with the better regular-season record
  e <- east$champ; w <- west$champ
  score_e <- -(wins[cbind(e, idx)] + runif(n, 0, 0.5))
  score_w <- -(wins[cbind(w, idx)] + runif(n, 0, 0.5))
  fin <- series_by_seed(e, score_e, w, score_w, P)
  rounds_won[cbind(fin$lose, idx)] <- 3L
  rounds_won[cbind(fin$win,  idx)] <- 4L

  tibble(
    sim          = rep(idx + sim_offset, each = n_teams),
    team_id      = rep(seq_len(n_teams), times = n),
    wins         = as.vector(wins),
    conf_rank    = as.vector(conf_rank),
    playoff_seed = as.vector(playoff_seed),
    # -1 = missed playoffs/lost play-in, 0 = lost R1, 1 = lost R2, 2 = lost conf finals,
    #  3 = lost Finals, 4 = champion
    rounds_won   = coalesce(as.vector(rounds_won), -1L)
  )
}
```

## Run the simulations

```{r run-sims}
set.seed(SEED)
t0 <- Sys.time()
starts <- seq(0L, N_SIMS - 1L, by = CHUNK)
sims <- bind_rows(lapply(starts, function(s) simulate_chunk(min(CHUNK, N_SIMS - s), s))) |>
  left_join(teams |> select(team_id = id, team, conf), by = "team_id")

# integrity checks: exactly one champion per sim, 8 playoff teams per conference per sim
stopifnot(
  n_distinct(sims$sim) == N_SIMS,
  all(sims |> group_by(sim) |> summarise(k = sum(rounds_won == 4)) |> pull(k) == 1),
  all(sims |> filter(!is.na(playoff_seed)) |> count(sim, conf) |> pull(n) == 8)
)

saveRDS(sims, SIMS_FILE)
cat(sprintf("%s simulated seasons x 30 teams = %s rows in %.1f s. Saved to %s\n",
            comma(N_SIMS), comma(nrow(sims)),
            as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "secs")), SIMS_FILE))
```

`sims` is a tidy table with one row per **team per simulation**: `wins`, `conf_rank` (1–15 by
regular-season record), `playoff_seed` (1–8 after the play-in, `NA` if missed), and `rounds_won`.
It is also saved to disk (`readRDS("nba_sims_2026.rds")`).

## Where the Knicks *should* have finished

```{r knicks-prep}
k_actual <- actual |> filter(team == FOCUS_TEAM)
k_sims   <- sims |> filter(team == FOCUS_TEAM)
```

```{r knicks-wins}
ggplot(k_sims, aes(wins)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, fill = "#F58426", colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = k_actual$actual_wins, colour = "#006BB6", linewidth = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = k_actual$actual_wins, y = Inf, vjust = 1.5, hjust = -0.1,
           label = paste("Actual:", k_actual$actual_wins, "wins"), colour = "#006BB6") +
  labs(title = paste(FOCUS_TEAM, "- simulated regular-season wins"),
       x = "Wins", y = paste("Simulations (of", comma(N_SIMS), ")"))
```

```{r knicks-rank}
k_sims |>
  count(conf_rank) |>
  mutate(p = n / N_SIMS) |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(conf_rank), p)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#F58426") +
  geom_point(data = tibble(conf_rank = k_actual$actual_conf_rank, p = 0),
             shape = 25, size = 4, fill = "#006BB6") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  labs(title = "Knicks' simulated Eastern Conference finish",
       subtitle = "Blue triangle = actual finish (by wins)",
       x = "Conference rank", y = "Probability")
```

```{r knicks-summary}
tibble(
  Metric = c("Actual regular-season wins",
             "Mean simulated wins",
             "P(simulated wins ≥ actual)",
             "Actual East rank (by wins)",
             "Mean simulated East rank",
             "Most likely East rank",
             "P(finish as East #1 seed)",
             "P(finish in East top 2)",
             "P(make playoffs - top 6 or play-in win)",
             "P(win the East)",
             "P(win the title)"),
  Value = c(k_actual$actual_wins,
            round(mean(k_sims$wins), 1),
            percent(mean(k_sims$wins >= k_actual$actual_wins), 0.1),
            k_actual$actual_conf_rank,
            round(mean(k_sims$conf_rank), 2),
            as.integer(names(which.max(table(k_sims$conf_rank)))),
            percent(mean(k_sims$conf_rank == 1), 0.1),
            percent(mean(k_sims$conf_rank <= 2), 0.1),
            percent(mean(!is.na(k_sims$playoff_seed)), 0.1),
            percent(mean(k_sims$rounds_won >= 3), 0.1),
            percent(mean(k_sims$rounds_won == 4), 0.2))
) |> kable()
```

## Was the title an anomaly?

Everyone's title probability (with Monte Carlo standard errors):

```{r title-odds}
title_odds <- sims |>
  group_by(team, conf) |>
  summarise(mean_wins    = mean(wins),
            p_playoffs   = mean(!is.na(playoff_seed)),
            p_finals     = mean(rounds_won >= 3),
            titles       = sum(rounds_won == 4),
            p_title      = titles / N_SIMS,
            se           = sqrt(p_title * (1 - p_title) / N_SIMS),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(p_title))

title_odds |>
  transmute(Team = team, `Mean wins` = round(mean_wins, 1),
            `Make playoffs` = percent(p_playoffs, 0.1),
            `Reach Finals` = percent(p_finals, 0.1),
            `Win title` = percent(p_title, 0.1),
            `± SE` = percent(se, 0.1),
            `Titles (of sims)` = titles) |>
  kable()
```

```{r title-plot}
title_odds |>
  mutate(team = reorder(team, p_title),
         focus = team == FOCUS_TEAM) |>
  ggplot(aes(team, p_title, fill = focus)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#F58426", `FALSE` = "grey70")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Simulated championship probability", x = NULL, y = NULL)
```

```{r anomaly-metrics}
p_k    <- title_odds$p_title[title_odds$team == FOCUS_TEAM]
rank_k <- which(title_odds$team == FOCUS_TEAM)
# probability that the champion in a typical season is a team with title odds <= the Knicks'
p_longshot <- sum(title_odds$p_title[title_odds$p_title <= p_k])

# how often does the *actual-looking* season arise: Knicks as champion AND outside East top seed, etc.
p_champ_not1 <- mean(k_sims$rounds_won == 4 & k_sims$conf_rank > 1) / max(mean(k_sims$rounds_won == 4), 1e-12)
```

* The model gives the Knicks a **`r percent(p_k, 0.1)`** chance to win the title
  (**#`r rank_k`** of 30 teams). That is about **1 in `r round(1 / p_k)`**.
* In a typical simulated season, the champion is a team with title odds at or below the Knicks'
  roughly **`r percent(p_longshot, 0.1)`** of the time, so a champion like the Knicks is
  `r if (p_longshot > 0.25) "not especially surprising" else if (p_longshot > 0.10) "somewhat surprising" else "genuinely surprising"`
  by this model.
* When the Knicks do win the title in the simulations, they were the East's #1 seed
  **`r percent(1 - p_champ_not1, 0.1)`** of the time.

::: {.callout-note}
## Interpreting "anomaly"
Ratings come from the same 82 games used to define the regular-season standings, so the model's
*mean* Knicks win total will sit near their actual total. The interesting question is the **spread**:
how many different seasons could have plausibly happened for the same underlying team quality? The title
probability is the cleanest summary of that. A ~`r percent(p_k, 0)` chance isn't an anomaly for
*any one team*; it's the same kind of thing as a team with a 10–15% pre-season number winning. See the
"champion's probability" check above for league-wide context.

Also note the model doesn't capture playoff-specific effects (shortened rotations, star usage,
injuries, in-season roster changes). A team that was truly better in the playoffs than its
regular-season rating suggests will look "lucky" here.
:::

## Seeds and championships

How likely is each **playoff seed** (1–8, after the play-in, pooled across both conferences) to win a round, reach the Finals, and win the title?

```{r seed-table}
seed_tbl <- sims |>
  filter(!is.na(playoff_seed)) |>
  group_by(playoff_seed) |>
  summarise(
    team_seasons = n(),
    p_win_r1   = mean(rounds_won >= 1),
    p_conf_finals = mean(rounds_won >= 2),
    p_finals   = mean(rounds_won >= 3),
    p_title    = mean(rounds_won == 4),
    titles     = sum(rounds_won == 4),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(share_of_all_titles = titles / N_SIMS)

seed_tbl |>
  transmute(Seed = playoff_seed,
            `Win R1` = percent(p_win_r1, 0.1),
            `Reach conf finals` = percent(p_conf_finals, 0.1),
            `Reach Finals` = percent(p_finals, 0.1),
            `Win title (a given team with that seed)` = percent(p_title, 0.1),
            `Share of all titles` = percent(share_of_all_titles, 0.1)) |>
  kable()
```

```{r seed-plot}
seed_tbl |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(playoff_seed), p_title)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#006BB6") +
  geom_text(aes(label = percent(p_title, 0.1)), vjust = -0.4, size = 3) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(title = "P(win the title) by playoff seed",
       subtitle = "Per-team probability, pooled across both conferences",
       x = "Playoff seed (after play-in)", y = NULL)
```

And by team: how often does each team land each playoff seed?

```{r seed-heatmap}
seed_by_team <- sims |>
  mutate(seed_lab = if_else(is.na(playoff_seed), "Out", as.character(playoff_seed))) |>
  count(team, conf, seed_lab) |>
  mutate(p = n / N_SIMS)

seed_by_team |>
  mutate(seed_lab = factor(seed_lab, levels = c(as.character(1:8), "Out"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(seed_lab, reorder(team, p * (seed_lab == "1")), fill = p)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "#006BB6", labels = percent) +
  facet_wrap(~conf, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Playoff seed", y = NULL, fill = "Probability")
```

## Reusable queries

Everything above can be regenerated from the saved `sims` table. A few helpers for later:

```{r helpers}
# P(team wins title | team lands a given playoff seed)
title_given_seed <- function(team_name, seed) {
  d <- sims |> filter(team == team_name, playoff_seed == seed)
  c(n = nrow(d), p_title = mean(d$rounds_won == 4))
}

# Which team wins the most titles?
title_odds |> slice_head(n = 5) |> select(team, titles, p_title)

# Title odds by (conference rank) instead of playoff seed
sims |>
  filter(conf_rank <= 10) |>
  group_by(conf_rank) |>
  summarise(p_title = mean(rounds_won == 4), .groups = "drop") |>
  kable(digits = 4)

# Finals matchups
# (not tracked explicitly; extend simulate_chunk() to return fin$win / fin$lose if you want these.)
```

## Notes and caveats

* **Ratings are static** across the whole season and playoffs, and the model ignores injuries, rest days, and rosters changing mid-season.
* **Seeding tiebreakers** are random rather than the official NBA rules.
* **Home-court advantage** is one league-wide constant (also used in the playoffs). It can be extended to team-specific home advantage with a second set of parameters.
* `PARAM_UNCERTAINTY <- FALSE` reproduces the "point-estimate only" version, which will give much more concentrated (and overconfident) title odds. Comparing the two is a good robustness check.
* To use margin of victory instead of win/loss, replace the logistic fit with a normal (point-spread) model; the simulation engine's structure stays the same.
